leading_catalyst: NVIDIA forecast about $11 billion of Q2 revenue as generative-AI demand accelerated, far above prevailing expectations.
caveat: QQQ also rallied 2.43%, but NVDA still outperformed it by 21.94 percentage points. Historical volume is vendor-reported and reflects later stock splits.

leading_catalyst: Quarterly revenue rose 265% year over year and the outlook reinforced that demand for AI accelerators continued to exceed expectations.
caveat: A strong QQQ session amplified the absolute move; the benchmark-adjusted move remained exceptional.

leading_catalyst: A broad semiconductor and AI-valuation selloff accelerated after soft U.S. manufacturing data; no single issuer announcement explains the regular-session fall.
caveat: This is an ambiguous control case. The reported DOJ subpoena story was published after the regular close and should not be used as the cause of the 9.52% daytime decline.

leading_catalyst: DeepSeek-R1's apparent capability and efficiency triggered doubts about the amount of high-end compute required by leading AI models.
caveat: The trigger attribution is strong, but whether efficient models reduce or expand aggregate compute demand was unresolved; the fundamental interpretation is less certain than the price attribution.

leading_catalyst: An SEC filing disclosed that Berkshire Hathaway had accumulated an approximately 11.4% stake in HP.
caveat: The filing cleanly explains the trading shock, but an ownership disclosure is not direct evidence of improved operating fundamentals.

leading_catalyst: HP cut its full-year adjusted EPS range after revenue missed expectations amid a slower PC recovery and weak demand in China.
caveat: The broad technology benchmark rose, strengthening the case for a stock-specific earnings attribution.

leading_catalyst: Revenue and adjusted EPS edged above expectations, while Personal Systems revenue returned to year-over-year growth and signaled a PC-market recovery.
caveat: Printing revenue remained weak, so the bullish interpretation rested mainly on Personal Systems and the recovery signal.

leading_catalyst: HP missed profit expectations and cut its annual EPS outlook to reflect tariff-related costs, moderated demand and macroeconomic uncertainty.
caveat: Tariff policy was changing quickly, so the durability of the earnings impact was less certain than the immediate attribution.

leading_catalyst: Intel reported weak results and outlook, announced a $10 billion cost-reduction plan and major workforce cuts, and said it would suspend the dividend.
caveat: A weak U.S. payroll report and broad risk-off session amplified the decline, but the 23.69-point QQQ underperformance was overwhelmingly company-specific.

leading_catalyst: Meta issued weak growth guidance and disclosed Facebook's first sequential decline in daily active users, while highlighting competition and Apple's privacy changes.
caveat: The technology market also sold off sharply, but Meta underperformed QQQ by 22.34 percentage points. The ticker was FB at the event date and later changed to META.

leading_catalyst: Bard's launch material contained a factual error and Google's presentation was judged against Microsoft's competing AI-search announcements, raising doubts about Google's response to generative AI.
caveat: Do not encode the Bard error as the sole cause. The move also reflected Microsoft's AI-search offensive, an underwhelming presentation and a weak technology session.

leading_catalyst: Azure growth and the cloud outlook failed to clear elevated expectations while investors questioned the near-term return on heavy AI infrastructure spending.
caveat: Headline revenue and EPS beat expectations; the negative reaction centered on Azure and forward-looking expectations, not an across-the-board earnings miss.

leading_catalyst: Apple cut quarterly revenue guidance to about $84 billion and attributed most of the shortfall to Greater China and weaker iPhone demand.
caveat: Apple's warning also drove a broad global-growth selloff, so QQQ is partly downstream of the same catalyst rather than a fully independent control.

leading_catalyst: Amazon reported a $3.8 billion quarterly net loss, including a $7.6 billion Rivian valuation loss, and gave weak operating-income guidance amid excess capacity and higher costs.
caveat: Inflation and a 4.50% QQQ decline amplified the absolute loss; AMZN still lagged QQQ by 9.55 percentage points. Historical prices and volumes reflect the later 20-for-1 split.

leading_catalyst: Salesforce's quarterly revenue missed expectations and its next-quarter revenue and profit guidance disappointed amid weak enterprise software spending.
caveat: This record has the sample's highest relative volume at 18.28 times the prior 20-session median.

leading_catalyst: Adobe beat quarterly expectations and raised annual targets as adoption of AI-enabled creative tools supported demand.
caveat: The release supports a stronger outlook, but separating AI enthusiasm from the ordinary earnings beat requires more granular analyst-expectation data.

leading_catalyst: Large AI contracts, a double-digit fiscal-2025 revenue-growth forecast, an OpenAI workload and a Google Cloud partnership outweighed a quarterly earnings miss.
caveat: A softer inflation report lifted QQQ, but ORCL still delivered 12.01 percentage points of excess return. Several same-package positives make single-claim attribution inappropriate.

leading_catalyst: A faulty Falcon sensor content update caused widespread Windows system crashes and disrupted airlines, banks, healthcare and other customers globally.
caveat: The operational trigger is certain; the eventual financial cost was not known on the event day, so price impact should not be equated with realized liability.

leading_catalyst: Broadcom reported 220% fiscal-year AI revenue growth and described a much larger future opportunity for custom AI accelerators and networking.
caveat: The share move embeds management's long-range opportunity framing, so its durability depended on future customer concentration and execution. Historical prices and volumes reflect the July 2024 stock split.

leading_catalyst: Micron's weak next-quarter revenue and profit forecast showed that soft PC and smartphone demand could outweigh near-term strength in AI and data-center memory.
caveat: The case is useful for ontology testing because positive AI demand and negative consumer-memory demand coexisted in the same release.
